sections.title: Types of MUN Committees
sections.content: MUN committees fall into three main types: General Assembly (GA) bodies with broad participation, Security Council (SC) with limited membership and veto power, and Crisis Committees that respond to fast-moving scenarios.
bullets: General Assembly: Large, all member states, two-thirds vote for resolutions
Security Council: 15 members, 5 permanent with veto power
Crisis: Small, fast-paced, responds to evolving situations

sections.title: Committee Flow
sections.content: A typical committee session flows through: Opening of session, Roll call, General Speakers List (GSL), Formal debate, Moderated/Unmoderated caucuses, Introduction of draft resolutions, Voting procedure, and Closing.
bullets: GSL comes first — delegates state their country's position
Caucuses follow — moderated for specific topics, unmoderated for negotiation
Draft resolutions are submitted, debated, amended, and voted on

sections.title: Committee Flow Chart
sections.content: Roll Call → GSL Speeches → Moderated Caucus → Unmoderated Caucus → Draft Resolutions → Amendments → Voting → Closing
sections.explanation: This is the typical flow. Each stage has specific rules and purposes. Knowing the flow helps you plan when to speak and when to negotiate.

sections.instruction: Which MUN body has permanent members with veto power?
sections.feedback: The Security Council has 5 permanent members (P5) who can veto substantive resolutions.

sections.q: What is the purpose of the General Speakers List (GSL)?
options: To allow delegates to state their country's position at the start of committee
sections.explain: GSL gives each delegate time to outline their country's stance on the topic. It opens the substantive portion of committee.

sections.statement: Amendments to draft resolutions can only be proposed during unmoderated caucus.
sections.feedback: Amendments can be proposed during formal debate, usually after the resolution has been introduced.

sections.sentence: The {0} {1} is the main debating body where all member states participate and each has one vote.
sections.instruction: Fill in the two-word name of this MUN body.
sections.feedback: The General Assembly includes all member states with equal voting power.

questions.instruction: Put these committee stages in the correct order.
questions.feedback: Roll Call → Speeches → Caucuses → Resolutions → Voting

questions.q: What is the main difference between GA and SC in MUN?
options: GA is larger but SC has veto power
questions.feedback: GA includes all members with equal votes; SC has 15 members with P5 veto power.
